cells.tense: Present — you're here, and the weight is where you put it.
cells.verb: putting your strength under something so it holds for other people
cells.place: in what gets passed on — the practice, the gathering, the thing that outlasts any one of you
cells.ask: pick the one shared thing you'd most want to see come all the way through, and let a little more of your weight go there than it has been — because what you back has a way of finishing, and that's what people are drawn toward.
cells.core:
You're holding up something that isn't only yours. The money, the time, the showing up — it's going under a thing people share, and it's going there by measure: enough that it stands, not so much that it leans on you. You can feel the difference between propping and smothering, and you're on the right side of it.

That's working. The question it opens isn't whether to keep going. It's which of the things you're carrying you'd actually want to see finished.
cells.sheetLine: You're holding up what's shared, and it's standing on its own.

cells.tense: Future — you're bracing for a collapse that hasn't come.
cells.verb: pouring strength into something faster than it can take it
cells.place: in what gets passed on — the practice, the gathering, the thing that outlasts any one of you
cells.ask: before the next thing you give, check privately what's actually yours to give here — what's owed, what's fair, what someone else was already going to do — and give that much; what comes back is a thing that holds without you forcing it to.
cells.core:
You're holding this up as if it would fall the moment you let go. Somewhere ahead there's a version where it all comes apart because you weren't there, and you're already living in it — so you give before anyone asks, cover what nobody was short on, hold up the whole thing by yourself. The thing you're carrying has stopped getting a chance to stand.

What's missing isn't generosity. It's the quiet sense of how much is actually yours to put in.
cells.sheetLine: You're carrying the whole thing so hard it can't hold itself.

cells.tense: Past — you're still standing where the giving went nowhere.
cells.verb: keeping your strength to yourself when something shared could use it
cells.place: in what gets passed on — the practice, the gathering, the thing that outlasts any one of you
cells.ask: don't try to give again yet; instead finish one thing you half-committed to, all the way to its end, and let what that costs you tell you whether you're still in — and the strength starts flowing toward what's shared on its own.
cells.core:
You've got something to put under this and you're not putting it there. Somewhere behind you is a time you gave to something shared and it didn't carry — it went nowhere, or it wasn't held — and you're still taking your instructions from that. So the strength stays home. The thing that could use it goes without.

The capacity hasn't left. The willingness to put it between people has.
cells.sheetLine: You stopped holding up what's shared, and you're still standing where it fell.

cells.tense: Present — you've put the pen down in a thing you're already writing.
cells.verb: already holding something up for other people
cells.place: in what gets passed on — the practice, the gathering, the thing that outlasts any one of you
cells.ask: name, out loud, which of the things you keep going you actually chose to keep going — the one that's yours — and the holding stops being a reflex and becomes something you're pointing.
cells.core:
You're already the reason this keeps happening. You pay for it, host it, show up early, cover the gap — and you'd say it runs itself, or that it's just what people do. It doesn't run itself. You're under it.

The holding is real and it's doing real work. What's missing is you saying that this is something you chose, so that you get to say what it's for.
cells.sheetLine: You're already holding it up. You just call it how things are done.
